note: Compiled from the registry per issue #588 Phase 1. A MechanicCandidate here is a transfer *obligation*, not a validated improvement. None of these has been implemented, evaluated or promoted. 'independent_evidence' is NONE for every entry in v1 because no reproduction has been attempted.

mechanics.preconditions: A cheap, automatable experiment whose outcome is machine-scoreable, so a search tree can be expanded without human adjudication at each node.
mechanics.mechanism: Progressive agentic tree search over experiment branches, arbitrated by a dedicated experiment-manager agent that decides which branch to expand next.
mechanics.claimed_benefit: Removes dependence on human-authored code templates and generalizes across ML domains.
mechanics.cost: Branch expansion multiplies compute; the branching factor is the dominant cost term. CANNOT_CHECK for exact figures.
failure_modes: Node scoring becomes the de facto objective, so a weak node scorer silently redirects the whole search.
Reported weakness at generating genuinely novel high-impact hypotheses persists despite the search.
mechanics.scope: Machine-learning experimentation; transfer to non-executable scientific domains is unestablished.
mechanics.rakl_analogue: ORION branch/candidate selection. RAKL already forbids treating a search score as evidence, so the transferable part is the manager's *allocation* policy, not its scoring authority.
mechanics.candidate_transfer_obligation: Build a challenger that adopts branch-allocation-under-budget while keeping RAKL's evidence gate; falsifier is that allocation gain vanishes once node scores are stripped of authority.

mechanics.preconditions: A single cheap held-out scalar that is a faithful proxy for the goal, and experiments short enough that many can run sequentially.
mechanics.mechanism: Propose a modification, run a short evaluation, keep it only if the held-out scalar improves, otherwise discard; repeat indefinitely.
mechanics.claimed_benefit: Reported 700 experiments in 2 days yielding 20 additive optimizations and an 11% training-time reduction, from ~630 lines of code.
mechanics.cost: One short training run per proposal; trivially parallel but strictly sequential in the reference implementation.
failure_modes: Single-scalar acceptance is structurally incapable of representing non-compensatory objectives - the exact failure RAKL's hard gates exist to prevent.
Additive-only accumulation cannot escape a local optimum that requires a temporarily worse intermediate.
No provenance or assurance separation whatsoever.
mechanics.scope: Narrow: ML pretraining with a fast reliable validation signal. Issue #588 explicitly declines to treat this as a general scientific-agent baseline.
mechanics.rakl_analogue: The ungoverned limit case of Self-RAKL mechanic evolution. Its value to ORION is as a control arm, not a mechanic to adopt.
mechanics.candidate_transfer_obligation: Register as the ungoverned control arm for Phase 4. The transfer question is inverted: does RAKL governance cost throughput relative to this loop on a task where the loop's preconditions actually hold?

mechanics.preconditions: Workflows are first-class editable objects and a fitness signal exists over their outputs.
mechanics.mechanism: The system writes, runs and mutates its own multi-agent workflows, selecting survivors by LLM-judge scores in a learning mode.
mechanics.claimed_benefit: Reported end-to-end autonomous reproduction of a 2018 molecular network analysis from raw instrument files in one command.
mechanics.cost: Population-scale workflow execution; CANNOT_CHECK for figures.
failure_modes: The fitness function is an LLM judge, which is precisely the routing-signal-as-evidence error RAKL's design constitution C1 forbids.
Darwinian selection over a judge signal is a direct path to evaluator gaming and meta-overfit.
mechanics.scope: Bioinformatics/omics pipelines in the reported case.
mechanics.rakl_analogue: Self-RAKL mechanic evolution. This is the closest external system to ORION's own recursive layer and therefore the most informative comparator in the registry.
mechanics.candidate_transfer_obligation: Faithful-transfer challenger: workflow-level mutation with an LLM-judge fitness, run to see whether it gains or gates-fails. Repaired challenger: same mutation operator with the fitness replaced by a RAKL evidence gate. The contrast between the two is the actual experiment.

mechanics.preconditions: Tools are exposed as discoverable services with machine-readable interfaces.
mechanics.mechanism: Scientific tools are published as MCP services and discovered at run time rather than being wired in ahead of time.
mechanics.claimed_benefit: The agent's tool set is not fixed at design time.
failure_modes: An expanding tool surface widens the authority boundary that must be audited.
Tool descriptions are author-controlled text and are an injection surface.
mechanics.rakl_analogue: ORION's operator basis. Run-time tool discovery is a way to grow the operator basis without a code change, which interacts directly with operator-basis-exhaustion claims.
mechanics.candidate_transfer_obligation: Determine whether operator-basis exhaustion claims survive a run-time-extensible basis, or whether exhaustion is only ever definable relative to a frozen basis.

mechanics.preconditions: A domain with checkable consistency laws (dimensional analysis, conservation, stoichiometry) that a checker can apply without solving the problem.
mechanics.mechanism: Hierarchical reflection checks intermediate and final outputs against physics-grounded consistency rather than against a generic self-critique prompt.
mechanics.claimed_benefit: Up to +7.5 percentage points over the strongest baseline at about one third of Gemini Deep Research's inference cost.
mechanics.cost: Reported to *reduce* net cost by avoiding wasted downstream work.
failure_modes: Self-paired benchmark/system release - the gain is not independently replicated.
Only applies where domain laws are cheap to check; degenerates to generic self-critique elsewhere.
mechanics.rakl_analogue: RAKL falsifier-bearing verification. This is the strongest positive-transfer candidate in v1: a cheap domain-law checker is evidence-bearing in a way an LLM judge is not.
mechanics.candidate_transfer_obligation: Highest-priority assimilation candidate. Transfer as a cheap invariant-checker stage; falsifier is that the gain disappears once RAKL's existing gates already catch the same errors.

mechanics.preconditions: Tasks recur with shared domain structure but differing specifics.
mechanics.mechanism: Two memory granularities held separately - reusable task experience and reusable domain knowledge - rather than one undifferentiated store.
failure_modes: Cross-task memory is a contamination route: experience from an evaluation task can leak into a later evaluation.
Granularity boundary is a design choice with no stated selection rule.
mechanics.rakl_analogue: RAKL fiber/experience reuse and the RAKL_RESET / RAKL_SHAM_MEMORY arms.
mechanics.candidate_transfer_obligation: Test whether splitting ORION memory by granularity beats the undifferentiated store under a matched budget, with the contamination check run first.

mechanics.preconditions: Intermediate outcomes are observable before the task ends.
mechanics.mechanism: Replan after each intermediate outcome instead of committing to an initial plan.
mechanics.claimed_benefit: Component of the reported DelveAgent gain; not separately ablated in the material read.
mechanics.cost: One planning call per intermediate outcome.
failure_modes: Not separately ablated, so its individual contribution is unknown.
Frequent replanning is a known route to instruction drift, one of the five failure modes named in the open-ended-research case studies.
mechanics.rakl_analogue: ORION route-switch latency and residual-driven re-planning.
mechanics.candidate_transfer_obligation: Requires an ablation before it can be treated as a distinct mechanic at all; currently confounded with MEC-DOMAIN_GROUNDED_REFLECTION.

mechanics.preconditions: A fixed literature corpus and search tool that every compared agent uses identically.
mechanics.mechanism: An agent environment that pins the retrieval corpus and search tooling, so retrieval quality stops being a hidden confounder between systems.
mechanics.claimed_benefit: Reproducible evaluation in which architectural differences are not confounded by corpus access.
mechanics.cost: Requires adapting ORION's retrieval path to the environment's interface.
failure_modes: Pinning the corpus removes exactly the capability difference that a retrieval-strong system would otherwise demonstrate; it measures reasoning-given-retrieval, not research capability.
mechanics.rakl_analogue: The matched-resource contract required by issue #588 Phase 4.
mechanics.candidate_transfer_obligation: This is the single highest-value *infrastructure* adoption in v1: it is what makes an ARCHITECTURE_CAUSAL_ELIGIBLE arm actually causal on the literature route. Adopt before any Tier 1 literature comparison is claimed.

mechanics.preconditions: Per-call cost is instrumented for every compared system.
mechanics.mechanism: Report capability against inference cost as a frontier rather than as a single ranked score; HAL implements the same idea with a shared scaffold and API-level cost tracking.
mechanics.claimed_benefit: Prevents a ranking that is really a budget difference in disguise.
failure_modes: Cost parity is not capability parity; equal spend across systems with different unit economics is still not a matched contract.
mechanics.rakl_analogue: Issue #588 Phase 5 efficiency QoIs and the Phase 8 Pareto frontier criterion; this mechanic is effectively already mandated by the issue's no-scalar-ranking rule.
mechanics.candidate_transfer_obligation: Adopt as the reporting format for every ORION-versus-external result. This is a reporting obligation, not a research candidate.
